title: This seems to be the teaching of the Roman Catechism (on the first article of the Creed; Wisdom 8:1)
source_text: XI. Quae videtur esse Doctrina Catechismi ipsius Romani Tridentini Concilii jussu in lucem editi, cujus haec Verba sunt in explicatione Symboli ad primum articulum sub finem. Non solum Deus Universa quae sunt providentia sua tuetur atque administrat, Verum etiam quae moventur & agunt aliquid, intima Virtute ad motum atque actionem ita impellit; ut quamvis causarum secundarum efficientiam non impediat, praeveniat tamen: cum ejus occultissima vis ad singula pertineat, & quemadmodum sapiens testatur, Attingat a fine usque ad finem fortiter, &c.
pass_a_gloss: Which seems to be the Doctrine of the very Roman Catechism put forth by order of the Council of Trent, whose Words are these in the explanation of the Creed on the first article towards the end. God not only protects and administers by his providence All things that are, But also those which are moved and do something, he so impels by an inward Power to motion and action; that although he does not hinder the efficiency of second causes, yet he prevents it: since his most hidden force reaches to each thing, and as the wise man testifies, Reaches from end to end mightily, &c.
pass_b_english: This appears to be the teaching of the Roman Catechism itself, published by order of the Council of Trent. Toward the end of its explanation of the first article of the Creed it says:

'God not only protects and governs by his providence everything that exists. He also so drives the things that move and act, by an inward power, to their motion and action that, while he does not hinder the efficiency of secondary causes, he goes before it, since his most hidden power reaches to every single thing and, as the wise man testifies, "reaches mightily from one end to the other", and so on.'

choices.why: Kept as the Thomist technical term; Le Blanc explains 'physical' as opposed to 'moral', not to 'supernatural'.
